manualReview.item: AP-06 may be folded into AP-01 at dedup: same root window, documentation only. Kept separate so it stays visible.

Seeded AM price (0.8452 sUSDS, about $0.942) is above annihilate parity (2*P_phUSD - 1, about $0.884). Holders get more by selling AM into the protocol pool than by annihilating ($23.24 vs $21.85 per 25 AM), so the protocol's LP absorbs claimant selling at a price above what AM redeems for. Intended per story-113 L113 ('AM/sUSDS opens at the existing phUSD/sUSDS market price, not at a $1 peg'). No arbitrage loop exists (test_r44_07: -$14.71).

AP-01 severity: Medium vs High. Theft is fork-proven without hypotheticals once AM circulates, and the runbook explicitly permits A-before-B. The value at stake is bounded at about $2.3k (the 10% slice).
Antimatter, UniPoolerV2 deployed bytecode is not Etherscan-verified (closure manifest 'unresolved'). Fork behaviour matched the nested-pin source in every path exercised.

Operator deleting the progress file mid-sequence (not instructed for any landed state) would re-size and rescue a second 10% slice to OWNER. No AM double-mint, because the exact-amount approval blocks it. Operator-error only.
Script C (uniswap-helper) was not executed against the AP-03 spoofed book; the downstream claim (C wires to the attacker's pair) is inferred from C's documented precondition (story-122 L148).
